subject: chem
title: Chemical Kinetics
syllabus: Rate of a chemical reaction; factors affecting rate: concentration, temperature, pressure and catalyst; elementary and complex reactions; order and molecularity; rate law, rate constant and its units; differential and integral forms of zero and first order reactions, their characteristics and half-lives; effect of temperature on rate; Arrhenius theory, activation energy and its calculation; collision theory of bimolecular gaseous reactions (no derivation).

body:
Rate = how fast concentration changes. For aA + bB → cC + dD:
rate = −\f{1}{a}\f{Δ[A]}{Δt} = −\f{1}{b}\f{Δ[B]}{Δt} = \f{1}{c}\f{Δ[C]}{Δt} = \f{1}{d}\f{Δ[D]}{Δt}
Dividing by the coefficient makes the rate one number for the whole reaction. In 2N_{2}O_{5} → 4NO_{2} + O_{2}, NO_{2} forms twice as fast as N_{2}O_{5} disappears.
Average rate uses a time interval; instantaneous rate is the slope of the tangent on a [A]–t curve.

Rate law (found by EXPERIMENT, not from the equation):
rate = k[A]^{x}[B]^{y}, order = x + y
Orders can be 0, fractions or negative. For an elementary step the order equals the molecularity.
Find order from data: change one concentration, keep others fixed: (concentration factor)^{order} = rate factor.
Unit of k = (mol L^{−1})^{1 − n} s^{−1}: zero order mol L^{−1} s^{−1}, first s^{−1}, second L mol^{−1} s^{−1}.
Mechanisms: the SLOW step decides the rate. A fast equilibrium before it lets you replace an intermediate, e.g. [A] = √{K[A_{2}]} → half orders.

check.q: k has unit L mol^{−1} s^{−1}. Order :

body: [A] falls as a STRAIGHT LINE with slope −k; the reaction finishes completely at t = [A]_{0}/k = 2t_{1/2}.
Examples: decomposition of NH_{3} on hot platinum, HI on gold — the surface is saturated so concentration does not matter.

General half-life rule:
t_{1/2} ∝ [A]_{0}^{1 − n}
— zero order ∝ [A]_{0}, first order constant, second order ∝ 1/[A]_{0}.

check.q: Zero order, t_{1/2} = 1 h at 2 M. Time for 0.5 → 0.25 M :

body: Half-life does NOT depend on the starting amount: every half-life halves what is left. After n half-lives (½)^{n} remains.
Radioactive decay is first order: carbon dating, ^{65}Zn, ^{82}Br, drug expiry (50% left) all use the same formula.
Rate = k[A], so rates at two times are in the same ratio as concentrations: \f{r_{1}}{r_{2}} = e^{kΔt}.
For a gas reaction in a closed vessel, total pressure changes as A turns into products. Let x = pressure of A used up.
At the end (t = ∞) all A is gone: P_{∞} = (moles of gas per A) × P_{0}. Use it to find P_{0}.

Then
k = \f{2.303}{t}log\f{P_{0}}{p_{A}}
e^{−E_{a}/RT} is the FRACTION of collisions with energy ≥ E_{a}. Rule of thumb: +10 °C roughly doubles k near room temperature.
Plot ln k vs 1/T: straight line, slope −E_{a}/R (for log k the slope is −E_{a}/2.303R), intercept ln A.
A catalyst lowers E_{a} (same A): ln\f{k_{cat}}{k} = \f{ΔE_{a}}{RT}. It does not change ΔH or the equilibrium.
Composite constants: if k = \f{k_{1}k_{2}}{k_{3}} then E_{a} = E_{1} + E_{2} − E_{3}; a square root halves everything.

traps: Order comes from experiment, never from the balanced equation (unless the step is elementary).
Rate of formation of NO_{2} ≠ rate of the reaction — divide by the coefficient.
First-order half-life is independent of concentration; zero-order half-life is proportional to it.
Volume does not change the rate — concentration does. Diluting does.
log k vs 1/T slope is −E_{a}/2.303R, not −E_{a}/R.
Use P_{∞} to get P_{0} when the reaction is started with pure A.
A catalyst changes the speed, not the equilibrium constant.

steps.note: Rate, rate law, order and units of k
Zero and first order, half-life and pressure data
Arrhenius equation, activation energy and catalysts

pyq.q: Rate law for a reaction between A and B is given by r = k[A]^{n}[B]^{m}. If concentration of A is doubled and concentration of B is halved from their initial value, the ratio of new rate of reaction to the initial rate of reaction (\f{r_{2}}{r_{1}}) is

Consider the following data for the given reaction 2HI(g) → H_{2}(g) + I_{2}(g). [HI] (mol L^{−1}): 0.005, 0.01, 0.02; Rate (mol L^{−1} s^{−1}): 7.5 × 10^{−4}, 3.0 × 10^{−3}, 1.2 × 10^{−2}. The order of the reaction is ______.

During kinetic study of reaction 2A + B → C + D, the following results were obtained: I. [A] = 0.1 M, [B] = 0.1 M, rate = 6.0 × 10^{−3}; II. [A] = 0.3 M, [B] = 0.2 M, rate = 7.2 × 10^{−2}; III. [A] = 0.3 M, [B] = 0.4 M, rate = 2.88 × 10^{−1}; IV. [A] = 0.4 M, [B] = 0.1 M, rate = 2.40 × 10^{−2} (initial rate of formation of D, M min^{−1}). Based on above data, overall order of the reaction is ______.
sol: Order in A: I → IV, [B] fixed, [A] ×4, rate ×4 → first order in A.
Order in B: II → III, [A] fixed, [B] ×2, rate ×4 → second order in B.

pyq.q: Consider the following reaction A + B → C. The time taken for A to become 1/4^{th} of its initial concentration is twice the time taken to become 1/2 of the same. Also, when the change of concentration of B is plotted against time, the resulting graph gives a straight line with a negative slope and a positive intercept on the concentration axis. The overall order of the reaction is ______.
sol: t_{1/4} = 2t_{1/2} means every half-life is the same → constant half-life → first order in A.
[B] falling as a straight line with time → zero order in B.

pyq.q: The reaction A_{2} + B_{2} → 2AB follows the mechanism: A_{2} ⇌ A + A (fast, k_{1}, k_{−1}); A + B_{2} → AB + B (slow, k_{2}); A + B → AB (fast). The overall order of the reaction is :

Given below are two statements : Statement I : The rate law for the reaction A + B → C is rate (r) = k[A]^{2}[B]. When the concentration of both A and B is doubled, the reaction rate is increased "x" times. Statement II : A plot of concentration of reactant against time is a straight line starting at [R]_{0} with slope −k for a "y" order reaction. The value of x + y is ______.
sol: A straight-line fall of [R] with time (slope −k) is the zero-order law [R] = [R]_{0} − kt → y = 0.

pyq.q: Observe the following reactions at T(K). I. A → products. II. 5Br^{−}(aq) + BrO_{3}^{−}(aq) + 6H^{+}(aq) → 3Br_{2}(aq) + 3H_{2}O(l). Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am. The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of −\f{Δ[Br^{−}]}{Δt} at 10.10 am is 2 × 10^{−4} mol L^{−1} min^{−1}. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is 10^{−2} mol L^{−1}. What is the first order rate constant (in min^{−1}) of reaction I ?

NO_{2} required for a reaction is produced by decomposition of N_{2}O_{5} in CCl_{4} as by equation 2N_{2}O_{5}(g) → 4NO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g). The initial concentration of N_{2}O_{5} is 3 mol L^{−1} and it is 2.75 mol L^{−1} after 30 minutes. The rate of formation of NO_{2} is x × 10^{−3} mol L^{−1} min^{−1}, value of x is ______. (nearest integer)
sol: Rate of disappearance of N_{2}O_{5} = \f{3 − 2.75}{30} = 8.33 × 10^{−3} mol L^{−1} min^{−1}.

pyq.q: For a reaction A →(K_{1}) B →(K_{2}) C. If the rate of formation of B is set to be zero then the concentration of B is given by :
sol: Net rate of formation of B = K_{1}[A] − K_{2}[B].
Setting it to zero (steady state): K_{1}[A] = K_{2}[B] → [B] = (K_{1}/K_{2})[A].

pyq.q: A → product (First order reaction). Three sets of experiment were performed for a reaction under similar experimental conditions: Run 1 ⇒ 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A; Run 2 ⇒ 200 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A; Run 3 ⇒ 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A + 100 mL of H_{2}O added. The correct variation of rate of reaction is
sol: Rate = k[A] depends on CONCENTRATION, not on volume.
Run 3: diluted to 200 mL → [A] = 5 M → half the rate.

pyq.q: Consider the reaction aX → bY, for which the rate constant at 30 °C is 1 × 10^{−3} mol^{−1} L s^{−1}. Which of the following statements are true ? A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes 16 times. B. The reaction is a second order reaction. C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X. D. Decomposition of N_{2}O_{5} is an example of the above reaction. E. A plot of ln\f{[R_{0}]}{[R]} against time is a straight line through the origin for the above reaction.
sol: Unit mol^{−1} L s^{−1} = (mol L^{−1})^{1−n} s^{−1} with n = 2 → second order (B true).
For second order t_{1/2} = \f{1}{k[X]_{0}} depends on [X]_{0} (C false).
N_{2}O_{5} decomposition is first order (D false), and the ln plot is the first-order test (E false).
o: A, B, D and E Only

pyq.q: In a reaction A + B → C, initial concentrations of A and B are related as [A]_{0} = 8[B]_{0}. The half lives of A and B are 10 min and 40 min, respectively. If they start to disappear at the same time, both following first order kinetics, after how much time will the concentration of both the reactants be same?
Time required for completion of 99.9% of a First order reaction is ______ times of half life (t_{1/2}) of the reaction. (nearest integer)
Time required for 99.9% completion of a first order reaction is ______ times the time required for completion of 90% reaction. (nearest integer)
Consider the first order reaction R → P. The fraction of molecules decomposed in the given first order reaction can be expressed as
sol: [R] = [R]_{0}e^{−k_{1}t}, so the fraction LEFT is e^{−k_{1}t}.

pyq.q: The rate of first order reaction is 0.04 mol L^{−1} s^{−1} at 10 minutes and 0.03 mol L^{−1} s^{−1} at 20 minutes after initiation. Half life of the reaction is ______ minutes. (Given log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771) (nearest integer)
For a first order reaction A → B, [A] = 0.6500 M at t = 0, 0.0650 M at t = x min and 0.00065 M at t = 20 min. x = ______ min. (Nearest integer)
sol: 0.65 → 0.00065 is a 1000-fold fall in 20 min: kt = ln 1000 = 3 ln 10.

pyq.q: An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to (\f{1}{8}) and (\f{1}{10})^{th} of its initial concentration are t_{1/8} and t_{1/10} respectively. What is the value of \f{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} × 10 ? (log 2 = 0.3)
The ratio of \f{^{14}C}{^{12}C} in a piece of wood is \f{1}{8} part that of atmosphere. If half life of ^{14}C is 5730 years, the age of wood sample is ______ years.
The half-life of radioisotopic bromine-82 is 36 hours. The fraction which remains after one day is ______ × 10^{−2}. (Given antilog 0.2006 = 1.587) (nearest integer)

Drug X becomes ineffective after 50% decomposition. The original concentration of drug in a bottle was 16 mg/mL which becomes 4 mg/mL in 12 months. The expiry time of the drug in months is ______. Assume that the decomposition of the drug follows first order kinetics.
sol: 16 → 4 mg/mL is two half-lives (16 → 8 → 4) in 12 months.
t_{1/2} = 6 months, and the drug expires at 50% → 6 months.

pyq.q: If the half life of a first order reaction is 6.93 minutes then the time required for completion of 99% of the reaction will be ______ minutes. (Given : log 2 = 0.3010) (nearest integer)

Sucrose hydrolyses in acidic medium into glucose and fructose by first order rate law with t_{1/2} = 3 hour. The percentage of sucrose remaining after 6 hours is ______. (Nearest integer) (Given : log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771)
The half-life of ^{65}Zn is 245 days. After x days, 75% of original activity remained. The value of x in days is ______. (Nearest integer) (Given: log 3 = 0.4771 and log 2 = 0.3010)

Consider the following reaction, the rate expression of which is given below: A + B → C, rate = k[A]^{1/2}[B]^{1/2}. The reaction is initiated by taking 1 M concentration of A and B each. If the rate constant (k) is 4.6 × 10^{−2} s^{−1}, then the time taken for A to become 0.1 M is ______ sec. (nearest integer)
sol: A and B start equal and are used 1 : 1, so [A] = [B] at all times.
Rate = k[A]^{1/2}[A]^{1/2} = k[A] → behaves as first order.

pyq.q: Consider the two different first order reactions given below: A + B → C (Reaction 1); P → Q (Reaction 2). The ratio of the half life of Reaction 1 : Reaction 2 is 5 : 2. If t_{1} and t_{2} represent the time taken to complete 2/3^{rd} and 4/5^{th} of Reaction 1 and Reaction 2, respectively, then the value of the ratio t_{1} : t_{2} is ______ × 10^{−1} (nearest integer). [Given: log_{10}(3) = 0.477 and log_{10}(5) = 0.699]
sol: 2/3 complete → 1/3 left → ln 3. 4/5 complete → 1/5 left → ln 5.

pyq.q: Reaction A(g) → 2B(g) + C(g) is a first order reaction. It was started with pure A. Pressure of system: 160 mm Hg at t = 10 min and 240 mm Hg at t = ∞. Which of the following option is incorrect?
sol: At 10 min: 80 + 2x = 160 → x = 40 → p_{A} = 80 − 40 = 40 mm Hg (option 3 correct).
k = \f{1}{10}ln\f{80}{40} = 0.0693 min^{−1}, not 1.693 → option 1 is INCORRECT.
A first-order reaction only approaches completion asymptotically (option 2 is acceptable).
o: Rate constant of the reaction is 1.693 min^{−1}
The reaction never goes to completion
Partial pressure of A after 10 minute is 40 mm Hg
Initial pressure of A is 80 mm Hg

pyq.q: A(g) → B(g) + C(g) is a first order reaction. The total pressure is P_{t} at time t and P_{∞} at t = ∞. The reaction was started with reactant A only. Which of the following expression is correct for rate constant k ?

Consider the following first order gas phase reaction at constant temperature A(g) → 2B(g) + C(g). If the total pressure of the gases is found to be 200 torr after 23 sec. and 300 torr upon the complete decomposition of A after a very long time, then the rate constant of the given reaction is ______ × 10^{−2} s^{−1} (nearest integer) [Given : log_{10}(2) = 0.301]

Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at T(K) and is given by A(g) → B(g) + C(g). In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar A(g) is allowed to decompose at T(K). After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant (in min^{−1}) of the reaction? (log 2 = 0.3)
sol: 1 + x = 1.5 → x = 0.5 → p_{A} = 0.5 bar: one half-life in 100 min.

pyq.q: For the thermal decomposition of N_{2}O_{5}(g) at constant volume, 2N_{2}O_{5}(g) → 2N_{2}O_{4}(g) + O_{2}(g), the total pressure is 0.6 atm at t = 0 and 'x' at t = 100 s. Given: Rate constant for the reaction is 4.606 × 10^{−2} s^{−1}. x = ______ × 10^{−3} atm [nearest integer]
sol: First order in N_{2}O_{5}: kt = 4.606 = 2 × 2.303 → N_{2}O_{5} falls 100 times → p = 0.006 atm.
Decomposed 0.594 atm gives 0.594 atm N_{2}O_{4} + 0.297 atm O_{2}.

pyq.q: First order gas phase reaction A → B + C. p_{i} = initial pressure of gas A, p_{t} = total pressure of the reaction mixture at time t. Expression of rate constant (k) is

The following data were obtained during the first order thermal decomposition of a gas A at constant volume: A(g) → 2B(g) + C(g). Total pressure 0.1 atm at t = 0 and 0.28 atm at t = 115 s. The rate constant of the reaction is ______ × 10^{−2} s^{−1} (nearest integer)
Half life of zero order reaction A → product is 1 hour, when initial concentration of reactant is 2.0 mol L^{−1}. The time required to decrease concentration of A from 0.50 to 0.25 mol L^{−1} is :

For a given reaction R → P, t_{1/2} is related to [A]_{0} as given in table: [A]_{0} = 0.100 mol L^{−1}, t_{1/2} = 200 min; [A]_{0} = 0.025 mol L^{−1}, t_{1/2} = 100 min. Given: log 2 = 0.30. Which of the following is true? A. The order of the reaction is 1/2. B. If [A]_{0} is 1 M, then t_{1/2} is 200√{10} min. C. The order of the reaction changes to 1 if the concentration of reactant changes from 0.100 M to 0.500 M. D. t_{1/2} is 800 min for [A]_{0} = 1.6 M.
sol: Order does not change with concentration (C false).

pyq.q: For reaction A → P, rate constant k = 1.5 × 10^{3} s^{−1} at 27 °C. If activation energy for the above reaction is 60 kJ mol^{−1}, then the temperature (in °C) at which rate constant, k = 4.5 × 10^{3} s^{−1} is ______. (Nearest integer) Given : log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, R = 8.3 J K^{−1} mol^{−1}, ln 10 = 2.3

Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by 20 kJ mol^{−1}. If k_{1} and k_{2} are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at 300 K, then ln\f{k_{2}}{k_{1}} will be ______ (nearest integer) [R = 8.3 J K^{−1} mol^{−1}]
sol: k = Ae^{−E_{a}/RT} with the same A.

pyq.q: A → B (first reaction), C → D (second reaction). Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at 500 K is double of the same at 300 K. At 500 K, 50% of the reaction becomes complete in 2 hour. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at 500 K of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at 300 K is ______ × 10^{−1} hour^{−1} (Nearest integer).
sol: First reaction at 500 K: t_{1/2} = 2 h → k_{1} = 0.3465 h^{−1}.

pyq.q: For a reaction taking place in three steps at same temperature, overall rate constant K = \f{K_{1}K_{2}}{K_{3}}. If Ea_{1}, Ea_{2} and Ea_{3} are 40, 50 and 60 kJ/mol respectively, the overall Ea is ______ kJ/mol.
sol: Each K = Ae^{−E/RT}: multiplying constants ADDS their activation energies, dividing SUBTRACTS.

pyq.q: Consider the following transformation involving first order elementary reaction in each step at constant temperature: A + B ⇌ C (step 1 forward, step 3 backward), C → P (step 2). Activation energies: step 1 = 300, step 2 = 200, step 3 = Ea_{3} kJ mol^{−1}. If the overall rate constant of the above transformation (k) is given as k = \f{k_{1}k_{2}}{k_{3}} and the overall activation energy (E_{a}) is 400 kJ mol^{−1}, then the value of Ea_{3} is ______ kJ mol^{−1} (nearest integer)

Consider a complex reaction taking place in three steps with rate constants k_{1}, k_{2} and k_{3} respectively. The overall rate constant k is given by the expression k = √{\f{k_{1}k_{3}}{k_{2}}}. If the activation energies of the three steps are 60, 30 and 10 kJ mol^{−1} respectively, then the overall energy of activation in kJ mol^{−1} is ______. (Nearest integer)
sol: Taking logs: ln k = ½(ln k_{1} + ln k_{3} − ln k_{2}) → E_{a} = ½(E_{1} + E_{3} − E_{2}).

pyq.q: Consider A →(k_{1}) B and C →(k_{2}) D are two reactions. If the rate constant (k_{1}) of the A → B reaction can be expressed by the following equation log_{10} k = 14.34 − \f{1.5 × 10^{4}}{T/K} and activation energy of C → D reaction (Ea_{2}) is \f{1}{5}th of the A → B reaction (Ea_{1}), then the value of (Ea_{2}) is ______ kJ mol^{−1}. (Nearest Integer)
sol: Compare with log k = log A − \f{E_{a}}{2.303RT}: \f{E_{a1}}{2.303R} = 1.5 × 10^{4} K.

pyq.q: At 27 °C in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by 10 kJ mol^{−1}. The logarithm of ratio of \f{k (catalysed)}{k (uncatalysed)} is.... (Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)

The temperature at which the rate constants of the given below two gaseous reactions become equal is ______ K. (Nearest integer) X → Y: k_{1} = 10^{6}e^{−30000/T}; P → Q: k_{2} = 10^{4}e^{−24000/T}. Given: ln 10 = 2.303

Given below are two statements : R = 8.314 J K^{−1} mol^{−1} and 1 cal = 4.2 J. Statement I: When Ea = 12.6 kcal/mol, the room temperature rate constant is doubled by a 10 °C increase in temperature (298 K to 308 K). Statement II: For a first order reaction A → B, a plot of t_{1/2} (s) against [A]_{0} (mol L^{−1}) is a straight line through the origin with positive slope.
sol: II: first-order t_{1/2} = 0.693/k does not depend on [A]_{0} — the plot is a horizontal line. FALSE.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are : A. Factor e^{−Ea/RT} corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea. B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction. C. Increase in temperature by about 10 °C doubles the rate of reaction. D. Plot of log k vs \f{1}{T} gives a straight line with slope = −\f{Ea}{R}.
sol: A false: e^{−E_{a}/RT} is the fraction with energy EQUAL TO OR MORE than E_{a}.
B true. C true (the usual rule of thumb).
D false: slope of log k vs 1/T is −\f{E_{a}}{2.303R}; −E_{a}/R is the slope for ln k.

pyq.q: Consider the following statements related to temperature dependence of rate constants. Identify the correct statements. A. The Arrhenius equation holds true only for an elementary homogenous reaction. B. The unit of A is same as that of k in Arrhenius equation. C. At a given temperature, a low activation energy means a fast reaction. D. A and Ea as used in Arrhenius equation depend on temperature. E. When Ea >> RT, A and Ea become interdependent.
sol: A false: it also describes complex and heterogeneous reactions (with apparent E_{a}).
B true: e^{−E_{a}/RT} has no unit, so A has the unit of k. C true.
D false: A and E_{a} are treated as temperature-independent. E false: they are independent constants.

words: Catalyst
Substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
Activation
Kind of energy needed to start a reaction
Arrhenius
Scientist whose equation links rate constant and temperature
Half life
Time for half of a reactant to be used up
Order
Sum of powers of concentrations in a rate law
Molecularity
Number of molecules taking part in an elementary step
Elementary
Kind of reaction that happens in a single step
Rate
Change in concentration per unit time
Intermediate
Species formed in one step and used up in a later step
Collision
Theory that molecules must hit each other to react
Frequency
Kind of factor also called the pre exponential factor
Zero
Order of a reaction whose rate does not depend on concentration
First
Order of a reaction with a constant half life
Pseudo
Kind of first order reaction where one reactant is in large excess
